pr_title: clusterversion,storage: add explicit version for split user keys
pr_body:
Pebble ceased splitting user keys across multiple sstables in a single
level in cockroachdb/pebble@a860bbad. A Pebble format major version was
added in 22.1 to mark existing tables with split user that formed an
"atomic compaction unit" for compaction. The compaction to recombine the
split keys happens at a low priority within Pebble, so there is no
guarantee that these tables have been recombined.

Pebble range key support depends on having split user keys recombined.
As such, the Pebble migration to upgrade to a version that support range
keys must first perform a blocking migration to compact tables with
split user keys.

Currently, the Cockroach cluster version
`EnsurePebbleFormatVersionRangeKeys` ratchets the Pebble version through
both the split user keys migration, up to the version that supports
range keys. Strictly speaking, the Pebble format version migration will
take care of the sequencing.

However, to provide better visibility into the various Pebble
migrations, and to cater for the fact that the split user keys migration
may take some time to recombine the necessary tables, a dedicated
cluster version for the split keys migration is added. This dedicated
cluster version makes it unambiguous what's blocking the Cockroach
version finalization.

Release note (backward-incompatible change, ops change): A cluster
version is added to allow Pebble to recombine certain SSTables
(specifically, user keys that are split across multiple files in a level
of the LSM). Recombining the split user keys is required for supporting
the range keys feature.  The migration to recombine the SSTables is
expected to be short (split user keys are rare in practice), but will
block subsequent migrations until all tables have been recombined. The
`storage.marked-for-compaction-files` time series metric can show the
progress of the migration.

Close #84012.

issue_context.title: storage: block 22.2 upgrade on removal of marked-for-compaction files
issue_context.body:
#77634 added a cluster version that marked all files with user keys shared with neighbors in the same level for compaction. We need to add a 22.2 cluster version that upgrades the format major version to [`FormatMarkedCompacted`](https://github.com/cockroachdb/pebble/blob/d68c152233afe41c9d5a8bfd8a0f80f2ee5f9107/format_major_version.go#L87) to block the version upgrade on finishing compacting away all of those marked files.

After that cluster version, we're free to reuse the `MarkedForCompaction` bit for future migrations (eg, the table-filter/block-property-filter migration).

This sweep step will free us up to remove atomic compaction units and related code for the 23.1 release.




Jira issue: CRDB-17406

Epic CRDB-2624

Note to self, following a conversation with @jbowens.

Strictly speaking, we're ok here already, as we already have a [cluster version in place in Cockroach to enable range keys](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/a3f32958321dfcb130701037e3068284a4436a32/pkg/clusterversion/cockroach_versions.go#L295). This migration covers compacting out all of the split user keys, which must happen [_before_](https://github.com/cockroachdb/pebble/blob/63d5527944113188fe042ae4d284fd1bd76f2df1/format_major_version.go#L87) we ratchet up to the Pebble format version for range keys.

_However_, we'll want to add an explicit cluster version to make it obvious that Cockroach is upgrading the Pebble format version, and this version upgrade must wait for all marked tables to be compacted before proceeding. In practice, the migration should be short lived (we don't expect too many split keys), but we should be clear in any case.
